page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, alongside 4.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is provisioned with 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It lacks dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs and does not come bundled with local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, with stress-ng single-core compute scoring 2921.98, placing it in the top 25%. Geekbench single-core performance registers at 1612.0, representing an average tier. In contrast, multi-core and parallel throughput are naturally constrained by the dual-thread topology. Geekbench multi-core scores reached 2013.0, and multi-threaded stress-ng settled at 2926.09, both residing in lower percentile brackets. Clang software compilation (2134.0) and ray tracing (2384.0) both score in the bottom 10%.

Memory bandwidth measurements highlight 136.6 GB/sec for cached read operations, dropping to 31.59 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 23.42 GB/sec for writes. The PassMark memory test score of 1151.19 and PassMark database operations score of 1006.97 both place in the bottom 10%, reflecting memory channel limitations typical of small-footprint virtual instances. Network-adjacent tests show 2.82 GB/sec static web serving throughput and Redis SET throughput of 2.32 million operations per second.

In terms of resource efficiency, the instance provides cost-effective dedicated CPU execution for light tasks without the overhead of larger compute shapes. However, workloads requiring intensive multi-threading, large working memory sets, or extensive disk IOPS face clear bottlenecks. The configuration is primarily suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, small background utilities, and development or continuous integration pipelines that benefit from predictable AMD Zen 3 execution.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized instance offering 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical AMD EPYC 7B13 core (x86_64) and 4.0 GB of system memory. Lacking local storage and GPU hardware, the instance relies on remote network storage volumes. Benchmark metrics highlight strong single-core CPU throughput (stress-ng score of 2921.98), though overall multi-core computational density and memory bandwidth remain modest due to the 2-vCPU ceiling. With 2.82 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 2.32 million Redis SET operations per second, c2d-highcpu-2 provides a cost-effective, dedicated baseline suited for lightweight microservices, single-threaded batch processing, and CI/CD agent runners.
